newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia insurers must act to head off foreign firms.
newsitem.headline: Russia insurers must act to head off foreign firms.

text.p: Russia should take serious steps to develop its insurance market or surrender to foreign companies when they flood in in 1999, the chairman of Russia's insurance supervisory body Rosstrakhnadzor said late on Tuesday.
"The insurance market is in crisis and we can only hope that 1996 was the worst year," Valery Sukhov told a news conference.
In 1996 the volume of insurance premiums in Russia was 27.4 trillion roubles or 4.3 trillion roubles more than in 1995, he said.
But 1996 annual inflation of 22 percent meant 1996 was the first year since 1991 when premiums fell in real terms, he said.
The fall was mainly due to a 20 percent drop in voluntary insurance and 30 percent fall in personal insurance, he said.
The volume of compulsory insurance funded by the government rose by 70 percent, he said.
"In fact the volume of insurance services by Russian companies fell," Sukhov said. "Insurers' financial state continues to worsen."
The number of insurance companies fell to about 2,500 from some 2,800 at the start of the year, but the figure may be lower after companies file their annual reports by April 1, he said.
In 1997 some growth will start, mainly due to a rise in premiums from companies' property insurance, he said.
This is because the government has allowed firms to include insurance costs in production costs for tax purposes in the amount of one percent of annual sales, he said.
Property insurance premiums will grow at least twofold, Sukhov said.

"But this rate of growth is not enough," he said. "At this growth rate we shall catch with the current state of Western countries in 50 years. We shall never catch up with them unless we take more radical steps in developing the market."
Foreign companies are now prohibited from working directly in Russia under a 1994 agreement with the European Union. The agreement expires in 1999.

"We may appeal (to the government) to postpone the date, but it will be a sensible step only if we take adequate steps to develop our insurance market, to set up powerful national companies. If such effort is not taken we should be meekly preparing for 1999."
Some local brokers sell foreign insurance policies in Russia and although the trend is not massive it worries the government, Sukhov said.
The State Duma (lower house of parliament) has passed in a first reading a law prohibiting companies registered in Russia from being insured by foreign companies, he said.
